To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following dietary and lifestyle factors are associated with a lower risk of myocardial infraction: low intake of total and saturated fat; low intake of alcohol; low intake of cholesterol; low intake of sodium; low intake of red and processed meat; high intake of vegetables; high intake of fruit; high intake of fish; low intake of refined grains; high intake of whole grains; low intake of sugar-sweetened beverages; and high intake of nuts.

the risk of myocardial infarc- tion is low in men who have a diet that includes high amounts of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts and legumes; a low intake of red and processed meats; and a low intake of trans fats and saturated fat.

the following diet and lifestyle factors are associated with lower risk of MI in men: a diet rich in vegetables, fruits, fish, whole-grain bread and cereal products; low intake of red meat and butter; and low alcohol consumption; and that these factors are associated with a 50% lower risk of MI.

the study of the effects of low-risk diet and lifestyle interventions on the risk of coronary heart disease in a general population.
